$comment: Short durations, and an explicit reduced-motion contract.
Motion in a clinical interface has one job: showing that something moved from A to B
so the eye can follow it. Anything longer than about 200ms stops helping and starts
costing time on a screen someone uses two hundred times a shift.
prefersReducedMotion is not decoration. Vestibular disorders are real, and so is
using a tablet in a moving vehicle during outreach work (CP144).

easing.$comment: standard for most things; decelerate for entering, accelerate for leaving, so motion feels like it comes from and goes somewhere.

reducedMotion.$comment: What every duration collapses to when the OS asks for reduced motion. Not zero everywhere: 1ms keeps transitionend handlers firing, so state machines built on them do not silently stall.
